interviewcake_find-duplicate-optimize-fo.incorrectReason: Treats a prefix exactly at capacity as overcrowded, steering toward a value that may occur only once.

notes.explanation: Binary-search the value bounds using prefix counts. Count all entries at most middle; if this exceeds middle, keep the lower value bounds, otherwise move the lower bound above middle. Read the original array without sorting or changing it.
notes.correctness: Maintain an overfull prefix ending at upper and a non-overfull prefix ending at lower-1. Initially the first contains n+1 entries for n possible values and the empty prefix contains zero. The count comparison preserves these bounds. When lower equals upper, subtracting the two prefix counts shows that this single value occurs at least twice.
notes.walkthrough: For [1,3,4,2,3], start with bounds 1..4. At middle 2, exactly two entries are at most 2, so move lower to 3. At middle 3, four entries are at most 3, exceeding three available prefix values, so upper becomes 3. Return 3, leaving the input unchanged.

interviewcake_find-duplicate-optimize-fo.incorrectReason: Returns the cycle entry successor instead of its index; that successor need not be a duplicated value.

interviewcake_shuffle.incorrectReason: Swapping each slot with an unrestricted random slot is biased: for three distinct entries, 27 equal-probability choice streams cannot distribute equally over six permutations.

notes.explanation: Fill positions from right to left. At position i, choose an index uniformly from 0 through i with the supplied random source and swap that occurrence into position i.
notes.correctness: Before an iteration, the unfilled prefix contains exactly the remaining occurrences. Each has probability 1/(i+1) of entering position i. Later swaps only touch earlier positions, so the filled suffix is final. Multiplying these conditional probabilities gives 1/n! for every occurrence permutation.
notes.walkthrough: Start with [4,8,1]. At i=2, a supplied draw of 0 swaps the final occurrence with index 0, giving [1,8,4]. At i=1, a draw of 0 then gives [8,1,4]. Those choices have probability (1/3)*(1/2)=1/6. The actual draws may produce any of the six equally likely permutations; true denotes the judge validating distribution, multiplicities and mutation of the supplied array.

interviewcake_inflight-entertainment.incorrectReason: Preloading every duration allows a single movie entry to pair with itself.

interviewcake_kth-to-last-node-in-singly.incorrectReason: Copies the correct value into a new object instead of returning the required existing node identity.

interviewcake_matching-parens.incorrectReason: Returns the first closing parenthesis, ignoring nested pairs that must close before the supplied opener.

notes.explanation: Scan from the supplied opener, including that character. Increment depth for each opener and decrement it for each closer; return when a closer first brings depth back to zero.
notes.correctness: After consuming the designated opener, depth counts the still-unclosed openers within that outer pair, including the outer opener itself. Nested pairs increase and then decrease this count. The first return to zero therefore closes the designated opener rather than an inner pair.

interviewcake_permutation-palindrome.incorrectReason: Rejects every valid odd-length palindrome multiset with its permitted single odd-frequency center.

interviewcake_recursive-string-permutati.incorrectReason: Omits the empty string permutation, although the empty input has one valid permutation rather than zero.

notes.explanation: Count each distinct character, then build prefixes recursively. For every character with a positive remaining count, append it, recurse with that count reduced, and restore the count before exploring the next choice. Store complete strings in a set.
notes.correctness: At each recursion level, the remaining counts are exactly the unused occurrences of the original input. Every chosen character preserves that invariant, so a completed prefix is a valid permutation. Every valid permutation determines a sequence of available-character choices and is therefore generated. Choosing characters by value rather than occurrence gives one path for each distinct string, including the empty string at the initial base case.
notes.walkthrough: For ab, the initial counts are a:1 and b:1. Choosing a leaves only b, so the first branch emits ab. Restoring both counts lets the next branch choose b then a and emit ba. For an empty input, the initial empty prefix is already complete and the result contains the empty string.
notes.timeComplexity: O(n * n!) worst-case time for n distinct characters, including prefix and result-string construction; repeated characters reduce the number of distinct branches.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n * n!) result storage in the worst case. The recursion has depth O(n), and simultaneously retained immutable prefix strings can occupy O(n²) additional characters.

interviewcake_word-cloud.incorrectReason: Drops internal apostrophes and hyphens, splitting valid bank words such as contractions and hyphenated compounds.

notes.explanation: Match maximal tokens of ASCII letters joined by internal apostrophes or hyphens followed by more letters. Lowercase each matched token and increment a null-prototype dictionary, so ordinary words such as constructor cannot collide with inherited properties.
notes.correctness: The expression starts each token with at least one letter and extends it only through another letter block joined by one allowed connector. Each maximal token under the disclosed grammar is therefore matched once; separators are excluded. Lowercasing sends all permitted case variants to the same key, and one increment per match records exactly their occurrence count.
notes.spaceComplexity: O(n) result storage and O(n) auxiliary matched-token storage for n input characters; the regular-expression match call materializes the token array.
